quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Be + Past Participle
quests.faultySentence: The letter was wrote by the assistant this morning.
quests.correctedSentence: The letter was written by the assistant this morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: The passive voice is formed with 'be' plus the past participle, so the sentence needs 'was written', not the simple past form 'wrote'.
quests.nativeTip: The passive voice needs the past participle, not the simple past form — what is the participle of 'write'?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Be + Past Participle
quests.faultySentence: The new policy was announce during yesterday's meeting.
quests.correctedSentence: The new policy was announced during yesterday's meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: Regular verbs form the past participle with '-ed', so the sentence needs 'was announced', not the base form 'was announce'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'was', the verb needs its past participle form — what ending does a regular verb take?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Subject-Verb Agreement
quests.faultySentence: The award were presented to the winning team at the ceremony.
quests.correctedSentence: The award was presented to the winning team at the ceremony.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'the award' is singular, the passive verb should be 'was presented', not the plural 'were presented'.
quests.nativeTip: 'The award' is singular — does the passive 'be' verb match that?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Simple Past for Specific Past Time
quests.faultySentence: The building has been build in 1990.
quests.correctedSentence: The building was built in 1990.
quests.ruleExplanation: A specific past time like '1990' requires the simple past passive, so the sentence needs 'was built in 1990', not 'has been build'.
quests.nativeTip: The specific year '1990' signals a finished, specific time — does that call for present perfect or simple past passive?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Present Continuous Passive
quests.faultySentence: The new bridge is being constructing this year.
quests.correctedSentence: The new bridge is being constructed this year.
quests.ruleExplanation: The present continuous passive is formed with 'is/are being' plus the past participle, so the sentence needs 'is being constructed', not 'constructing'.
quests.nativeTip: The present continuous passive needs the past participle, not the -ing form — what's the correct form of 'construct'?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Future Passive
quests.faultySentence: By next year, the new stadium will completed.
quests.correctedSentence: By next year, the new stadium will be completed.
quests.ruleExplanation: The future passive is formed with 'will be' plus the past participle, so the sentence needs 'will be completed', not 'will completed'.
quests.nativeTip: The future passive needs a form of 'be' before the past participle — what's missing here?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Unknown or Unimportant Agent
quests.faultySentence: Someone stole my bike from outside the library last night.
quests.correctedSentence: My bike was stolen from outside the library last night.
quests.ruleExplanation: When the agent is unknown, the passive voice is more natural, focusing on what happened to the bike: 'my bike was stolen'.
quests.nativeTip: The person who stole the bike is unknown — is it more natural to focus on the unknown 'someone' or on what happened to 'my bike'?

quests.conceptTitle: Active Voice: Important or Emphasized Agent
quests.faultySentence: The report is written by the analyst every single month, so it's easy to identify her writing style in each one.
quests.incorrectPart: The report is written by the analyst every single month
quests.correctedSentence: The analyst writes the report every single month, so it's easy to identify her writing style in each one.
quests.correctedPart: The analyst writes the report every single month
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the analyst's identity and style are the focus, active voice highlighting the doer is more natural: 'the analyst writes the report'.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence emphasizes recognizing the analyst's specific writing style — does that call for passive or active voice, which foregrounds the doer?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice: Unknown or Unimportant Agent
quests.faultySentence: They completed construction of the new hospital wing ahead of schedule.
quests.incorrectPart: They completed construction of the new hospital wing
quests.correctedSentence: Construction of the new hospital wing was completed ahead of schedule.
quests.correctedPart: Construction of the new hospital wing was completed
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the agent is vague and unimportant, the passive voice is more natural, focusing on the hospital wing: 'construction... was completed'.
quests.nativeTip: Who exactly 'they' refers to isn't specified or important here — is it more natural to focus on the vague 'they' or on the hospital wing itself?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice with Modals: Modal + Be + Past Participle
quests.faultySentence: This form must submitted before the deadline.
quests.correctedSentence: This form must be submitted before the deadline.
quests.ruleExplanation: Modal passives are formed with the modal plus 'be' plus the past participle, so the sentence needs 'must be submitted', not 'must submitted'.
quests.nativeTip: A passive modal needs a form of 'be' before the past participle — what's missing here?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice with Modals: Modal + Have Been + Past Participle
quests.faultySentence: The issue should have fixed before the product launched.
quests.correctedSentence: The issue should have been fixed before the product launched.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the issue receives the action rather than performing it, the sentence needs the passive form 'should have been fixed', with 'been' included.
quests.nativeTip: This describes something that should have happened to the issue, not something the issue did itself — is 'been' missing?

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice with Modals: Modal + Be + Past Participle

quests.ruleExplanation: The causative structure 'have something done' requires the past participle, so the sentence needs 'had her car repaired', not the base form 'repair'.

quests.conceptTitle: Causative: Have + Object + Past Participle

quests.correctedSentence: The company had its financial records audited by an outside firm.
quests.ruleExplanation: The causative structure 'have something done' requires the past participle, so the sentence needs 'had its financial records audited', not the base form 'audit'.

quests.conceptTitle: Causative: Make + Person + Bare Infinitive
quests.faultySentence: The manager made the intern to redo the entire report.
quests.correctedSentence: The manager made the intern redo the entire report.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Make' in the causative sense is followed by the bare infinitive, so the sentence needs 'made the intern redo', not 'to redo'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Make' causing someone to do something is followed by the bare infinitive, without 'to' — is 'to' needed here?

quests.conceptTitle: Causative: Let + Person + Bare Infinitive
quests.faultySentence: Our parents always let us to stay up late on weekends.

quests.conceptTitle: Causative: Have + Person + Bare Infinitive
quests.faultySentence: The professor had the students to submit their essays a week early.
quests.correctedSentence: The professor had the students submit their essays a week early.
quests.ruleExplanation: When 'have' causes a person to perform an action, it's followed by the bare infinitive, so the sentence needs 'had the students submit', not 'to submit'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Have' causing a person (not a thing) to do something is followed by the bare infinitive, without 'to' — is 'to' needed here?

quests.conceptTitle: Participle Clauses: Present Participle for Active Meaning
quests.faultySentence: Written the report quickly, she submitted it before the deadline.
quests.correctedSentence: Writing the report quickly, she submitted it before the deadline.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'she' actively wrote the report, the sentence needs the present participle 'writing', not the past participle 'written', which implies a passive meaning.
quests.nativeTip: Is 'she' doing the writing (active) or having something done to her (passive)? Which participle form fits an active meaning?

quests.conceptTitle: Participle Clauses: Past Participle for Passive Meaning
quests.faultySentence: Exhausting from the long shift, the nurse went straight home.
quests.correctedSentence: Exhausted from the long shift, the nurse went straight home.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the nurse experienced exhaustion caused by the shift, the sentence needs the past participle 'exhausted', not the present participle 'exhausting', which would mean she caused exhaustion in others.
quests.nativeTip: Did the nurse cause exhaustion, or did she receive/experience it from the shift? Which participle form fits a passive, receiving meaning?

quests.conceptTitle: Participle Clauses: Past Participle for Passive Meaning
quests.faultySentence: Interviewing by three different panels, the candidate felt confident about her chances.
quests.correctedSentence: Interviewed by three different panels, the candidate felt confident about her chances.

quests.nativeTip: Did the candidate do the interviewing, or was she interviewed by the panels? Which participle form fits a passive, receiving meaning?

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Participles: Matching the Implied Subject
quests.faultySentence: Walking through the park, the flowers looked beautiful.
quests.incorrectPart: Walking through the park, the flowers looked beautiful
quests.correctedSentence: Walking through the park, she thought the flowers looked beautiful.
quests.correctedPart: Walking through the park, she thought the flowers looked beautiful
quests.ruleExplanation: As written, the sentence illogically suggests the flowers were walking; a logical subject needs to be added, such as 'she thought the flowers looked beautiful'.
quests.nativeTip: Who is actually doing the walking? Can flowers walk through a park?

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Participles: Matching the Implied Subject
quests.faultySentence: Having finished the presentation, the questions from the audience began.
quests.incorrectPart: Having finished the presentation, the questions from the audience began
quests.correctedSentence: Having finished the presentation, the speaker took questions from the audience.
quests.correctedPart: Having finished the presentation, the speaker took questions from the audience
quests.ruleExplanation: As written, the sentence illogically suggests the questions finished the presentation; the logical subject, 'the speaker', needs to follow the participle phrase.
quests.nativeTip: Who actually finished the presentation? Can 'the questions' finish a presentation?

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Participles: Matching the Implied Subject
quests.faultySentence: After reviewing the contract carefully, several concerns were raised by the legal team.
quests.incorrectPart: several concerns were raised by the legal team
quests.correctedSentence: After reviewing the contract carefully, the legal team raised several concerns.
quests.correctedPart: the legal team raised several concerns
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'the legal team' did the reviewing, they should be the subject immediately following the participle phrase: 'the legal team raised several concerns', not the passive construction that leaves 'several concerns' as the subject.
quests.nativeTip: Who actually reviewed the contract — the concerns, or the legal team? The subject right after the comma should match the doer of the participle.
